UX/UI case study · Vendor mobile app

Zaaroz vendor app, redesigned to run a shop at a glance

Zaaroz vendors accept orders, manage menus and track payouts from one app, often mid-rush and one-handed. I redesigned the existing green app into a clearer, warmer and more guided experience.

RoleUX/UI designer (concept)
PlatformAndroid vendor app
ScopeDashboard, menu, payouts, reviews, store tools, support
ToolsFigma

Vendors needed answers fast; the app made them dig

The old app was functional, but dark green bars, small text and plain rows gave every element equal weight. In a busy kitchen or shop, that costs seconds on every action.

Flat

No visual hierarchy

Headers, totals and actions all looked alike, so nothing guided the eye.

Hidden

Tools buried in a grid

Grocery ordering, settlements and customer orders sat behind small icons on the Vendor Store tab.

Blank

Dead-end empty states

Screens ended with “Sorry, No Payment Found” or “No history to show yet” and no next step.

Vague

Money was hard to read

Sales and earnings were two small figures. There was no clear view of balance, payouts or what a vendor receives.

From audit to system

I started by auditing every screen of the existing app, then redesigned around a few clear goals.

AuditReviewed each old screen for hierarchy, clarity and consistency.
Define goalsGlanceable status, clear money, guided states.
RestructureGroup tools, add a branch switcher, simplify navigation labels.
Design UINew color, type, cards and illustrated empty states.
SystemiseOne component set across all flows.

Design system

Orange now means “do something”. It marks primary buttons, active tabs and key highlights. Green is kept for positive states like Available and Paid, so each color has one job.

Old header
Primary
Tint
Canvas
Text
AreaBeforeAfter
ColorDark green bars, orange buttons competingWarm orange primary on cream, green for status only
LayoutPlain rows and large tilesRounded cards with spacing that groups information
Empty statesText onlyIllustrations with guidance on the next step
ConfirmationsGeneric dialogsDelete Item states the consequence with clear primary and secondary actions
FlowsLimited support and ordering screensAdded Add Item, Add Ticket, grocery browsing with delivery or pickup, and bill details before payment

Outcome and how I would measure it

The redesign gives the vendor app a clear hierarchy, one consistent visual system and helpful states from first launch to payout.

This is a self-initiated concept redesign, so there is no usage data yet. Here is how I would prove it works once vendors try it.

MeasureHow to measure itWhat success looks like
Time to accept an orderTime from the new-order alert to the accepted tap, in a vendor testShorter than in the old app
Price-update completion rateShare of vendors who change an item price without helpHigher, with fewer wrong taps
Time to find a toolAsk vendors to open grocery orders or settlements from the Vendor Store tabFaster, with fewer wrong turns
Payout support ticketsCount of tickets about payouts and balancesFewer tickets over time
Vendor satisfactionA short SUS survey after each versionHigher score for the new design

Next steps

  • Test the dashboard and menu flows with real vendors.
  • Check contrast and touch-target sizes for outdoor, one-handed use.
  • Extend the system to tablet and dark mode.
